description: RootShift is a team passionate about using NASA Earth observation data and technology to build innovative solutions for climate-resilient agriculture. We aim to help farmers make smarter crop rotation decisions, adapt to changing environmental conditions, and promote sustainable farming for the future.
summary:
RootShift is an interactive agricultural decision-support platform developed to help farmers make more informed crop-rotation decisions in the face of changing environmental conditions.

Users select their farm location through an interactive map, provide relevant farm information such as soil type and irrigation, and access location-specific environmental data from NASA POWER. Through the Rotation Lab, farmers can enter their existing crop rotation and create two alternative rotations of their own choice. RootShift brings these scenarios together for comparison, helping users understand potential benefits, risks and environmental trade-offs.

Rather than automatically generating crop rotations, RootShift keeps farmers in control of their decisions while making scientific environmental information more accessible and practical.

Our goal is to support climate-conscious agricultural planning, encourage informed decision-making and contribute to more resilient farming practices.
details:
What RootShift does

RootShift is a crop-rotation comparison and agricultural decision-support platform. It helps users evaluate their existing crop rotation against two alternative rotations they select themselves.

The application begins with an interactive map where users identify their farm location. Users then provide relevant farm information, including soil type and irrigation details. Using the selected coordinates, RootShift retrieves daily environmental data through NASA's Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) API.

In the Rotation Lab, users enter their current crop rotation and construct two alternative crop-rotation scenarios. The platform brings together the available environmental information, farm context and crop characteristics to help users examine and compare their options.

Benefits and intended impact

RootShift aims to make environmental information more accessible to agricultural decision-making. By allowing farmers to compare different rotation scenarios, it encourages consideration of climate conditions, water availability, soil characteristics and potential agricultural trade-offs.

Its intended impact is to support more informed crop-planning decisions, improve awareness of environmental risks and contribute to climate-resilient agricultural practices.

Technology and tools

The project was developed using:

  • Python — application logic and data processing.
  • Streamlit — interactive web application.
  • NASA POWER Daily API — environmental data retrieval.
  • Requests — API communication.
  • Pandas — processing and organizing environmental time-series data.
  • Interactive map technology — farm location selection.
  • Pytest — application testing.

Creativity and considerations

RootShift combines location-specific environmental information with a farmer-driven comparison workflow. Instead of automatically recommending or generating crop rotations, it allows farmers to construct their own alternatives and explore the differences between them.

The project considers location, environmental data availability, soil and irrigation context, crop characteristics, data limitations and uncertainty. It aims to present environmental information transparently rather than treating estimates as guaranteed agricultural outcomes.
